findings.claim: The whole of lesson 4 teaches the Catholic route: marriage as one of the seven sacraments, Catechism 2360-2365, 'Not Just Good But Beautiful' (Pope Francis 2014), Familiaris Consortio 36-85, the Family Group Movement and Catechism 2226. The lesson description opens 'Catholic teaching on marriage as a sacrament'.
findings.truth: Those are the named sources of Area of Study 3A (Catholic Christianity), not 3B (Christianity), which this unit teaches. Section 2 of 3B names Mark 10:6-9 (purpose of marriage), 1 Corinthians 6:7-20 (sexual relationships), Ephesians 6:1-4 (purpose of the family) and Matthew 19:13-14 plus Sunday schools (support in the local parish). None of those appear anywhere in lesson 4. The raw text of this lesson is byte-identical to lesson 4 of the sibling unit religious-studies-edexcel/paper-3-philosophy-ethics-catholic, so the Catholic lesson was copied into the Christianity unit. The fix is a rebuild of lesson 4 against 3B 2.1-2.4, keeping Catholic teaching only as one of the divergent Christian views. It is not surgical, so no edit is written.
findings.evidence: spec 3B section 2 (2.1-2.4) vs spec 3A section 2 (2.1-2.4); diff of raw/L04.txt against the Catholic unit's raw/L04.txt is empty
findings.ruling: REBUILD ITEM for Tom: wrong-route lesson copied from the Catholic unit; too large to patch in the loop. Other items: fix in the Catholic unit / unverified.

findings.claim: The whole of lesson 5 teaches the Catholic route: annulment and Catechism 2382-2386, Catechism 2207 and 'the dignity of work within the home', the theology of the body, and Catechism 1938. The lesson description opens 'Catholic teaching on contraception, divorce...'.
findings.truth: Those are the named sources of Area of Study 3A, not 3B. Section 2 of 3B names Matthew 19:1-12 (divorce and remarriage), Genesis 1-3 and Ephesians 5:21-30 (equality of men and women) and Galatians 3:23-29 (gender prejudice). Annulment is not part of 3B at all. Only Humanae Vitae and situation ethics are shared between the two routes. The raw text is byte-identical to lesson 5 of religious-studies-edexcel/paper-3-philosophy-ethics-catholic. The fix is a rebuild against 3B 2.5-2.8. Not surgical, so no edit is written.

findings.claim: Catechism 1938 states that 'every form of social or cultural discrimination in fundamental personal rights on the grounds of sex, race, color, social conditions, language, or religion must be curbed and eradicated as incompatible with God's design.' The same wrong citation is repeated in knowledge check 4, flashcard 7 and the mark scheme of practice question 4.
findings.truth: That sentence is printed under Catechism 1935, not 1938. Catechism 1938 reads: 'There exist also sinful inequalities that affect millions of men and women. These are in open contradiction of the Gospel...'. The spec does name 1938 for this topic, so the paragraph number should stay but the quotation must be corrected. No edit is written here because lesson 5 needs rebuilding out of this unit; the identical wording sits in lesson 5 of the Catholic unit, where it is in scope and should be fixed.

findings.claim: the Family Group Movement, founded in France in 1947
findings.truth: The movement the spec names is the Passionist Family Groups Movement, which began in Australia in the early 1970s, not in France in 1947. I could not confirm the exact year and founder from an authoritative source (Wikipedia has no article and the movement's own site did not respond), so I have not written a correction. Either verify the founding date and country and correct it, or drop the date and country and describe the movement only by what it does. The same sentence sits in lesson 4 of the Catholic unit.

findings.claim: For the 12-mark Discuss question, remember to develop the Hume/Dawkins counter-argument in full - examiners note that students often write only one sentence on the opposing view.
findings.truth: Two errors. The command word for the 12-mark question in this qualification is 'Evaluate', not 'Discuss'; the spec says these abilities are rewarded in questions that use the command word 'Evaluate'. And 'examiners note that...' is an invented examiner claim with no source.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 command words (State 3, Outline 3, Describe 4, Explain 4 or 5, Evaluate 12)

findings.claim: Question 2 is set as '3 marks - Describe': 'Describe what Christians believe happened at the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:1-13).'
findings.truth: Paper 3 has two questions, each numbered (a) to (d): outline three (3), explain two (4), explain two with a source of wisdom and authority (5), evaluate (12). 3 + 4 + 5 + 12 = 24 per question, 48 for two, plus 3 SPaG marks = 51. There is no Describe question on Paper 3, and the spec gives Describe a 4-mark tariff. The mark scheme already awards three separate points, so the stem should be an outline-three question.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 3 assessment overview (50 minutes, 51 marks, two questions each (a)-(d)) and Appendix 3 command words

findings.claim: Question 5 is set as '12 marks - Discuss a Statement' and ends 'Discuss this statement.'
findings.truth: The 12-mark AO2 command word is 'Evaluate'. 'Discuss' is not a command word in this qualification. This label is used 71 times and '3 marks - Describe' 72 times across all 15 Edexcel Religious Studies units, so the same relabel is needed subject-wide.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 command words; grep of scripts/_retrofc/units/religious-studies-edexcel__*

findings.claim: For the 12-mark Discuss, develop the Dawkins/Humanist counter-argument fully
Question 2 is set as '3 marks - Describe'; question 5 is set as '12 marks - Discuss a Statement' and ends 'Discuss this statement.'
findings.truth: Paper 3 uses outline three (3), explain two (4), explain two with a source (5) and evaluate (12). Describe carries 4 marks in this spec and does not appear on Paper 3; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 3 assessment overview and Appendix 3 command words

findings.claim: Mark scheme for question 6 (a 5-mark source question): 'source credit for Romans 1:18-24 used in counter-framing, or Darwin cited explicitly (1)'.
findings.truth: The fifth mark is for referencing a source of wisdom or authority. Darwin's On the Origin of Species is not a religious source of wisdom and authority, so naming it does not earn that mark. The scriptural anchor for the design argument in this spec is Romans 1:18-24.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 (Explain, 5 marks: 'reference one source of wisdom or authority in support of their explanation'); spec 3B 1.6

findings.truth: Paper 3 uses outline three (3), explain two (4), explain two with a source (5) and evaluate (12). Describe carries 4 marks in this spec and does not appear on Paper 3; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: Mark scheme for question 6 (a 5-mark source question): 'source credit for Proverbs 22:6 in counter-argument framing, or Dawkins The God Delusion cited explicitly (1)'.
findings.truth: The fifth mark is for referencing a source of wisdom or authority. The God Delusion is not a religious source of wisdom and authority, so naming it does not earn that mark. The named source for religious upbringing in this spec is Proverbs 22:6.

findings.claim: The experience of worshipping, praying and hearing scripture as a child creates deep neural and emotional pathways that can anchor belief through the challenges of adulthood.
findings.truth: The neuroscience claim is asserted as fact and is not supported by any cited study. It is presented as part of the Christian case, so it does not cost marks, but it should be attributed rather than stated flatly if the lesson is ever revised.
findings.evidence: no source given in the lesson

summary: Lessons 4 and 5 are byte-identical copies of the Catholic route (Area of Study 3A) lessons and teach none of the scripture the Christianity route (3B) names, so half of this Paper 3 unit is the wrong option and needs rebuilding. Lessons 1 to 3 are factually sound on scripture, philosophers and dates, but all five lessons carry a subject-wide question-labelling error: 'Discuss' instead of the real command word 'Evaluate' at 12 marks, and a 3-mark 'Describe' question that Paper 3 does not have.
